messages:
Alyssa Park: Hey team, escalating a customer issue — their indexing job started failing after we rolled the new embeddings model yesterday. Customer sees "dimension mismatch" errors when writing vectors to their vecdb. They just switched to `redwood-embed-v2` on their end.

Jin Wu: Can you paste the error payload? Also which vecdb are they using?

Alyssa Park: They're on `VecStoreX` managed by our indexer. Error log: 
```
ERROR: indexer: write failed: expected_dim=1536, got_dim=1024, doc_id=acct-8621
```
They report previously using `redwood-embed-v1` (1536 dims). v2 returns 1024.

Marco Reyes: Ok that explains it — v2 changed dim. We should have surfaced model dim in the API response metadata, but also indexer should reject gracefully and not loop. Is the indexer still trying to backfill?

Alyssa Park: Yes, the indexer started a backfill of ~2M docs when they migrated schema. It looks like the backfill worker is retrying on each doc and hitting the mismatch every time. Backfill job id: `bf-2026-03-14-09`

Samira Khan: Customer contacted support — they're blocked: ingest rate dropped to zero and search degrades. They want a short-term fix and a safe plan for backfill.

Elliot (DB Admin): Quick mitigation: we can accept 1024 vectors by creating a new index alias `idx_acct-8621_v2` with dim=1024 and route writes from the backfill there, but search queries that expect 1536 embeddings will not match unless we re-embed queries or pad/transform.

Jin Wu: Before we make index changes, can we confirm what our embeddings API returns now? Alyssa: curl example?

Alyssa Park: Provided sample request from customer:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
{ "model": "redwood-embed-v2", "input": ["hello world"] }
```
Response:
```
{"data":[{"embedding":[0.001, -0.02, ...], "dimensions":1024}], "model":"redwood-embed-v2"}
```
No explicit `dimensions` field used to be present in v1 responses; v2 added dims but indexer isn't reading it.

Marco Reyes: Two immediate action items: 1) Support/ingest team — pause the backfill job to stop retries. 2) Eng-runtime/ingest — add a short fix to indexer to verify incoming dim and route to an alternate index or return a clear 4xx so backfill can fail fast and be retried with correct pipeline.

Samira Khan: Done: paused `bf-2026-03-14-09`. Notifying customer that ingestion paused and we're rolling a fix.

Jin Wu: For a quick fix, I can push a hotpatch to indexer: if embedding payload dims != index.dim -> respond 422 with message "dim_mismatch: expected=X got=Y; include model in body". That will make the backfill fail fast and let them re-run with correct model. Deploying to staging first.

DevOps-bot: deploy started: indexer-hotpatch-v2 -> staging (job 5823). Logs streaming at https://logs.redwood.internal/5823

Marco Reyes: Long-term, we should store `embedding_dim` in the model catalog and surface required_dim in the indexer config so migrations can be validated pre-flight. Also add an auto-compat mode for common dim changes (e.g., PCA downsampling) but that's opt-in.

Elliot (DB Admin): For their backfill, recommended plan:
- create new index with dims=1024: `idx_acct-8621_v2`
- run a small sample reindex to verify search quality (50k docs)
- if they need unified search, pick: re-embed queries with v2 or re-embed corpus with v1 (depending on latency/cost)
- schedule full backfill with rate limit 200 req/s to avoid OOMs

Alyssa Park: Customer asked if we can temporarily downsize v2 outputs to 1536 by padding — not safe. Upsampling/padding would be misleading. We should not auto-convert.

Samira Khan: Customer agreed to re-run backfill against new index alias. They asked for a short repro they can run locally to verify before re-ingesting.

Jin Wu: Repro steps for customer to verify dims before starting backfill: 
1) curl embeddings with their model: 
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-v2","input":["test"]}' | jq '.data[0] | {len: (.embedding|length), model: .model}'
```
2) Confirm length matches index expected dim (1536 vs 1024). 3) If mismatch, switch to `model=redwood-embed-v1` or create new index with correct dim.

Marco Reyes: Also adding a small telemetry event on write failures with reason `dim_mismatch` and the model id so we can detect other customers impacted.

DevOps-bot: deploy succeeded: indexer-hotpatch-v2 -> staging (job 5823). Runbook: https://runbooks.redwood/internal/indexer-dim-check

Samira Khan: Patch promoted to canary in prod — monitoring for error spikes. Customer notified and started verification.

Alyssa Park: Follow-up: customer completed sample run, confirmed embeddings are 1024 on v2. They created `idx_acct-8621_v2` and re-run a 50k doc trial — ingestion succeeded. They're scheduling full backfill next week.

Jin Wu: Postmortem notes: failure root cause = model upgrade changed embedding dimension; indexer lacked validation and surfaced ambiguous errors, causing backfill retries and amplified disruption. Action items: 
- model catalog: expose `embedding_dim` and enforce during model selection (owner: eng-ml)
- indexer: validate dims and return 4xx if mismatch + include model_id in error (owner: eng-platform)
- support: update KB with repro and hotpatch steps (owner: support)
- telemetry: emit `dim_mismatch` metric (owner: eng-sre)

Marco Reyes: I'll file the trackers and assign owners. Thanks all for quick turnaround. :tada:

Elliot (DB Admin): We'll coordinate index lifecycle and keep alias `idx_acct-8621` pointing to v1 until they confirm cutover.

Alyssa Park: Closing loop with customer and will follow up after full backfill. Thanks everyone.
